name: The Unreached (antiquity)
summary: Most of humanity in antiquity never hears the gospel; the dark warp behind the light.

name: The Unreached (medieval)
summary: Beyond Christendom's edges, the field stays dark for a thousand years.

name: The Unreached (early modern)
summary: Asia and the interior remain largely unreached before the missionary century.

name: Born after the conquest (MENA)
summary: After the 7th-c. conquests the Christian East becomes a shrinking minority.

name: Confucian-Buddhist world (Asia)
summary: Even amid modern missions, most of East Asia remains unreached.

name: Hindu world (South Asia)
summary: Christianity stays a small minority across the subcontinent.

name: Apostolic convert
summary: Hears an apostle or a neighbor, believes, and is baptized.

name: Martyr of the persecutions
summary: Refuses to recant; the blood of the martyrs becomes seed.

name: House-church matron
summary: Keeps a household church; the quiet backbone of the early church.

name: Constantinian nominal
summary: Joins when the faith becomes respectable; belief stays a label.

name: Desert ascetic
summary: Flees to the desert to seek God wholly.

name: Barbarian baptized with the king
summary: Converted top-down when the chieftain is baptized.

name: Monastic copyist
summary: Carries faith and letters through the dark centuries.

name: Medieval peasant believer
summary: Born into Christendom; devout in form, ordinary in fervor.

name: Orthodox faithful of the Rus
summary: Baptized with the Rus; Orthodoxy becomes the soul of a people.

name: Thomas Christian of Malabar
summary: An ancient church surviving on the Indian coast.

name: Reformation lay reader
summary: Reads Scripture in the vernacular and finds living faith.

name: Recusant martyr
summary: Dies for confession in an age of religious war.

name: New World mission convert
summary: Baptized en masse under colonial mission; faith folk and inherited.

name: Hidden Christian (Japan)
summary: Keeps the faith in secret across generations of persecution.

name: Pietist of the awakening
summary: Heart-religion rekindled in small renewal societies.

name: Great-Awakening convert
summary: Swept up in the colonial revivals.

name: Mission-school pupil (Africa)
summary: Learns to read Scripture at a mission school and believes.

name: Slave-convert of the diaspora
summary: Finds in the gospel both hope and a community in bondage.

name: First reader of a new translation
summary: The Bible arrives in the mother tongue; the church takes root.

name: Colonial nominal Christian
summary: Adopts the colonizer's religion as a label.

name: Pentecostal of Azusa
summary: Touched by the Pentecostal outpouring.

name: East African revivalist
summary: Confession and song turn a mission church into living faith.

name: Base-community Catholic
summary: Faith deepened in small grassroots communities.

name: Soviet secret believer (Lyudmila)
summary: Raised under atheism, lapses, then returns late through believing ties — the Lyudmila arc.

name: Soviet atheist (lost faith)
summary: State atheism severs an inherited faith.

name: Chinese house-church believer
summary: Comes to faith in a hidden church and stays despite pressure.

name: Korean megachurch convert
summary: Part of Korea's rapid 20th-c. growth.

name: Western nominal who drifts
summary: Inherited faith quietly thins to nothing.

name: Post-Christian seeker who returns
summary: After drifting, comes home through a crisis and a friend.

name: Global-South migrant believer
summary: Carries a vibrant faith along the routes of migration.
